messages.content: I’m moving on from Puget Sound. Can you help sketch the April Front Range swing? I’m looking at flying SLC to Colorado on Monday April 14 and home Thursday April 17. Events are Tuesday evening in Fort Collins, Wednesday 7:30 a.m. counselor breakfast in Boulder, Wednesday late afternoon transfer table in Aurora, then a Thursday morning high-school visit in Colorado Springs.

Yes. Before I shortlist it, two choices affect reliability: do you want the Wednesday 7:30 Boulder breakfast to be the protected point, or would you rather avoid a late Tuesday drive after Fort Collins? And is Thursday home-by-dinner important enough to risk a tighter return?

Protect Wednesday morning. The Fort Collins reception is supposed to end around 8:15, and I can drive after that if it makes the breakfast calmer. Thursday I’d like to be back by dinner, but not with a silly connection. Delta is nice if it works, but I’d rather not make the route fragile.

Got it. I’d treat Denver as the main airport and Colorado Springs as a possible return only if the times are clean. For the hotels, the first-night zone is the real trade-off: Fort Collins is easiest Tuesday night, Boulder is easiest Wednesday morning, and Longmont is the middle ground.
Breakfast and parking matter too. I’ll have a rental car, and after that Tuesday reception I don’t want to discover there’s nowhere easy to grab food.

Then Longmont is probably the practical first pick. It keeps Tuesday night from becoming a full Boulder drive, makes the Wednesday breakfast reachable in about 25-35 minutes in normal morning traffic, and chain hotels there are more likely to include breakfast and parking than central Boulder.
Can you compare Fort Collins, Longmont, and Boulder plainly? I keep talking myself into all three.

Short version: Fort Collins means easiest dinner/bed after the reception, but you would need a very early departure for Boulder, likely around 6:00. Boulder means the calmest 7:30 breakfast, but a longer late Tuesday drive plus higher rates and parking fees. Longmont is not perfect, but it spreads the inconvenience: about 40-50 minutes after Fort Collins, then 25-35 minutes to Boulder.
What about the Wednesday Aurora table and Thursday Colorado Springs visit? I don’t want to solve one morning and create a worse one.

That points to a split stay. I’d pencil Longmont for Monday and Tuesday nights, then move south after the Aurora table on Wednesday. South Denver/DTC, southeast Aurora, or Castle Rock would all beat staying north for the Colorado Springs morning. DTC is the safest balance for dinner, hotels, and highway access.
Would you put me in Colorado Springs Wednesday night instead?

Only if the Aurora table ends early enough. Aurora to Colorado Springs after an event can be 75-100 minutes, and dinner gets less flexible if you arrive late. DTC or Castle Rock lets you get south of Denver without committing to the whole drive after a long Wednesday.
Okay. For flights, is there any reason to return from Colorado Springs instead of just Denver round trip?

There could be, but I’d be cautious. Denver round trip gives you nonstop choices SLC-DEN both ways and simpler car pricing. Colorado Springs return avoids the drive back north, but many COS-SLC options connect through DEN, PHX, or DFW. If the Thursday visit runs long, a COS connection can become the fragile piece.
The Thursday school visit starts at 9 and should be done by 10:45. I could leave Colorado Springs by 11 if no one needs extra time.

Then a late-afternoon Denver return is probably better than a midday Colorado Springs connection. From Colorado Springs to DEN, budget 90 minutes driving plus rental return and security. A Denver departure around 4:30-5:30 gives you a real cushion; earlier than 3:30 would feel rushed.
What would your rough itinerary be before we price actual flights and hotels?

Monday: afternoon nonstop SLC-DEN, pick up the rental at DEN, drive to Longmont, sleep there. Tuesday: use Longmont as the base, then Fort Collins reception, return to Longmont after. Wednesday: leave Longmont around 6:40 for Boulder breakfast, check out beforehand if possible, drive to Aurora for the transfer table, then sleep DTC or nearby south Denver. Thursday: drive to Colorado Springs, finish the visit, return the car at DEN, fly home late afternoon.
If we end up in Boulder because rates drop, does that change the airport recommendation?

No. Boulder would make Wednesday morning easier but does not change the flight logic. I’d still use DEN round trip unless Colorado Springs has a clean, well-timed one-stop with a comfortable connection and a fare that justifies the extra moving parts.
Give me the shortlist to research tonight.

Research these three paths: 1) Best balance: DEN round trip, Longmont Monday-Tuesday, DTC/south Denver Wednesday. 2) Maximum Wednesday-morning comfort: DEN round trip, Boulder Monday-Tuesday if under cap and cancellation is reasonable, DTC Wednesday. 3) Lowest late-Tuesday effort: Fort Collins Monday-Tuesday, then DTC Wednesday, but only if you accept a very early Boulder departure. For hotels, check breakfast start time, parking cost, cancellation deadline, and whether there is food open after 9 p.m. near the Longmont or Fort Collins property.

messages.content: Front Range update: Fort Collins moved later. It is now 7:15 to 9 p.m. Tuesday, and Aurora wants me set up by 2:15 Wednesday. Boulder hotels near the breakfast are either over cap or have bad cancellation. Longmont has a couple breakfast-included rates, and south Denver has more normal pricing.

That makes the split stay stronger. With the reception ending at 9, I would not push all the way to Boulder unless the hotel is clearly worth it. And with Aurora setup at 2:15, staying north all the way through Wednesday starts to work against you.
So rank it for me. Option A is two north-side nights so I do not have to change hotels Wednesday morning. Option B is Longmont then south Denver, which means one more checkout.

My ranking: 1) Longmont Tuesday night, then south Denver/DTC Wednesday night. 2) Longmont both Tuesday and Wednesday only if avoiding the checkout matters more than Thursday morning reliability. 3) Boulder Tuesday night only if the rate comes under cap with flexible cancellation. I would drop Fort Collins now because the Wednesday breakfast is too early.
Why DTC over Aurora? The transfer table is in Aurora.

If the Aurora hotel is right by the venue and has easy dinner, it can work. I lean DTC because it usually has more business hotels, easier restaurant choices, and a cleaner start toward Colorado Springs Thursday. East Aurora can add awkward cross-town driving in the morning.

The Longmont holds are Home2 at $156 and Hampton at $168. Both say breakfast included and free parking. Home2 cancellation is 6 p.m. two days before; Hampton is day before. Boulder is $226 plus parking or prepaid at $201.

Use Longmont. The Boulder options either break the cap after parking or give up flexibility. Between the Longmont holds, Hampton has the better cancellation, but Home2 is cheaper and still flexible enough if you are comfortable deciding two days out. Verify breakfast start time; for a 7:30 Boulder breakfast, 6:00 is useful and 6:30 means grab-and-go.
South side choices: Hampton Denver Tech Center South at $159, Hyatt Place DTC at $174, and a Castle Rock Best Western at $149. All list breakfast. Parking looks free except Hyatt says maybe $8.

I’d rank Hampton DTC South first, Castle Rock second, Hyatt third. Hampton DTC keeps you close enough after Aurora, has likely restaurant options nearby, and gives a reasonable Thursday drive. Castle Rock shortens Thursday but makes Wednesday night more of a haul after a packed day. Hyatt is fine if the room or cancellation is better, but the possible parking fee weakens it.
Do I need to worry about dinner Tuesday after getting to Longmont?

A little. If the reception ends at 9, you may reach Longmont around 9:45 or 10 depending on where in Fort Collins it is. I’d either eat something at the reception, grab food before leaving Fort Collins, or pick a Longmont hotel near Ken Pratt/Main where late fast-casual options are more likely. Do not rely on a full restaurant after check-in without calling.
And breakfast Wednesday?

Call both Longmont hotels. Ask: what time hot breakfast starts on Wednesdays, whether coffee or packaged items are available earlier, and whether parking is truly included for all nights. If breakfast starts at 6, you can eat quickly and leave around 6:40. If it starts at 6:30, plan coffee/snack only and eat properly after the Boulder breakfast event.
What details should I verify before I let the holds expire?

Verify these in order: Longmont breakfast start time, Longmont cancellation deadline in local time, free parking language, and late check-in policy for Tuesday after 10 p.m. Then verify DTC breakfast start time for Thursday, parking fees, cancellation deadline, and restaurants within a short walk or five-minute drive. If all checks out, book Longmont for the north-side nights and Hampton DTC South for Wednesday.

messages.content: Fares are finally workable for Front Range, and my hotel holds expire tonight. Monday afternoon SLC-DEN nonstop is easy. The Colorado Springs returns all connect and feel tight after the Thursday school visit. Denver return is later Thursday afternoon but means driving back north. Help me choose and tell me what to book.

I’d like one timing check before picking the return: does the Colorado Springs visit still end around 10:45, and can you leave by 11:00 if needed? That determines whether the Denver drive is comfortable or just technically possible.
It is 9 to 10:45. I can probably leave at 11, but counselors sometimes keep me a few minutes. I do not want to sweat a 35-minute connection out of COS.

Then skip the Colorado Springs return. A connected COS itinerary adds exactly the risk you are trying to avoid. Use Denver round trip, keep the car the whole time, and choose the later Thursday DEN-SLC nonstop so the drive back from Colorado Springs has room for a delay, fuel stop, and rental return.
The flight choices I’m seeing are Delta Main SLC-DEN 1:20-2:47 Monday and DEN-SLC 5:05-6:38 Thursday for $238 round trip, or United for about $35 less but returning 4:15. Both are nonstop.

I’d take the Delta Main at 5:05. The extra 50 minutes Thursday is worth more than the $35 savings because your morning starts in Colorado Springs. Main Cabin also avoids the most annoying change and seat limitations that can come with basic fares.
Good. Can I request window seats without paying extra?

If the seat map has standard windows open, yes. For the Monday outbound, take a left-side window if available, something like 18A or 19A. For Thursday, any standard window is fine; 20F or 21F would work. If only paid preferred windows are left, skip the fee and set a check-in reminder.

Hotels on hold are Home2 Longmont Monday and Tuesday at $156, cancel by Saturday 6 p.m., breakfast included/free parking, and Hampton DTC South Wednesday at $159, cancel by Tuesday 6 p.m., breakfast/free parking. Does that match the route?

Yes. Home2 Longmont for Monday-Tuesday protects the Boulder breakfast without making Tuesday after Fort Collins awful. Hampton DTC South Wednesday keeps you positioned for Aurora dinner/logistics and the Thursday Colorado Springs drive. I would book both before the holds expire.
Rental car timing?

Book DEN pickup Monday around 3:15 p.m. That gives you time to deplane and reach the rental center after the 2:47 arrival. For Thursday, list the return around 2:30 or 3:00 p.m., even though the flight is 5:05. Personally aim to be at the rental return by 2:30; that gives a cushion if I-25 or the rental shuttle is slow.
Anything special on the car route? I may use toll roads if I’m late.

Choose the rental company’s toll option only if it is reasonable; otherwise save toll receipts or the final toll line item for reimbursement. E-470 can help depending on where you are in Aurora, but do not plan the trip around it. Also keep the fuel receipt if you have to refill near DEN.
Okay, final booking order and receipt list?

Book in this order: 1) Delta Main SLC-DEN Monday 1:20-2:47 and DEN-SLC Thursday 5:05-6:38; select standard window seats if open and save the airfare receipt. 2) DEN rental car, pickup about 3:15 Monday and return listed 2:30-3:00 Thursday. 3) Home2 Longmont for Monday-Tuesday, noting Saturday 6 p.m. cancellation, breakfast, and free parking. 4) Hampton DTC South for Wednesday, noting Tuesday 6 p.m. cancellation, breakfast, and free parking. Keep airfare receipt, hotel confirmations and folios, cancellation terms, rental estimate/final receipt, fuel, tolls, and any parking charges.
